prompt_examples.title: Non-compliant cross-border contract (UK company, employee working in Germany)
prompt_examples.note: A deliberately abusive contract. The Supervisor resolves both jurisdictions and the stated pay, Company Law (UK) and Employee Law (Germany) audit in parallel against their own statutes, the Supervisor validation gate filters the findings, and the Editor/Reflection loop rewrites every offending clause. This run returned 33 accepted breaches.

Company country: United Kingdom
Employee country: Germany
Contract / Offer text: EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

This Employment Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into on 1 January 2026 between:

ABC Technologies Ltd, a company incorporated in England and Wales with its registered office at 50 Innovation Street, London, EC2A 3AB, United Kingdom ("Company"),

and

Max Mustermann, residing at Musterstrasse 12, 10115 Berlin, Germany ("Employee").

The Company and the Employee are collectively referred to as the "Parties."

1. Position
The Employee shall be employed as a Senior Software Engineer.
The Employee shall report to the Engineering Manager or any other person designated by the Company.
The Employee agrees to perform any duties assigned by the Company that the Company reasonably believes fall within the Employee's abilities.
The Company reserves the right to change the Employee's job title, reporting structure, responsibilities, department, or role at any time without requiring the Employee's consent.

2. Employment Start Date
Employment shall commence on 1 February 2026.
The employment is intended to continue indefinitely unless terminated in accordance with this Agreement.
The first twelve (12) months shall constitute a probationary period during which the Company may terminate employment immediately without notice.

3. Place of Work
The Employee shall work remotely from Germany.
The Employee agrees that the Company may require relocation to the United Kingdom at any time upon providing fourteen (14) days' notice.
The Company may also require temporary work from any location worldwide if business needs require.

4. Working Hours
The Employee's normal working hours shall be Monday through Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM London time.
The Employee shall work no fewer than fifty (50) hours each week.
The Employee agrees to work additional hours whenever requested without additional compensation.
The Employee shall remain reachable by telephone, email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and WhatsApp between 8:00 AM and 10:00 PM UK time.

5. Salary
The Employee shall receive a gross annual salary of EUR 68,000.
Salary shall be paid monthly.
The Company may reduce the Employee's salary whenever business conditions require.
The Company may withhold salary if performance targets are not achieved.
The Company may recover accidental overpayments by deducting any amount from future wages without limitation.

6. Bonus
The Employee may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus.
The Company may cancel or modify the bonus program at any time.
The Company retains sole discretion over whether any bonus is paid.

7. Overtime
The Employee acknowledges that the salary includes compensation for all overtime regardless of the number of additional hours worked.
No overtime payments shall ever be made.

8. Vacation
The Employee shall receive twenty (20) days of paid annual leave.
Vacation must be approved in advance.
Unused leave expires automatically at the end of each calendar year.
The Company may cancel previously approved vacation whenever business requirements demand.
The Employee shall not take more than five consecutive working days of leave.

9. Sick Leave
The Employee must notify the Company before 8:00 AM on the first day of illness.
A doctor's certificate shall be provided for any illness lasting more than one day.
The Company is not required to pay salary during periods of sickness.
The Company may terminate employment if the Employee is absent due to illness for more than fourteen consecutive days.

10. Equipment
The Company shall provide a laptop, monitor, keyboard and mouse.
The Employee is responsible for all repairs regardless of fault.
The Employee shall reimburse the Company for any damaged equipment, including ordinary wear and tear.

11. Internet and Utilities
The Employee shall provide internet access suitable for work.
No reimbursement shall be provided for electricity, internet, heating, or office expenses.

12. Confidentiality
The Employee shall not disclose confidential information during employment or after termination.
Confidential Information includes source code, product plans, financial information, customer information, internal communications and business strategies.
This obligation survives indefinitely.

13. Intellectual Property
All inventions, software, documentation, ideas, improvements, discoveries, and creative works created by the Employee during employment or within five years after employment ends shall belong exclusively to the Company.
This includes works created entirely during the Employee's personal time using personal equipment.
The Employee waives all moral rights worldwide.

14. Data Protection
The Employee agrees that the Company may collect, process, monitor, store, analyze, and transfer all personal information worldwide for business purposes.
The Employee consents to continuous monitoring of emails, telephone calls, webcam, screen activity, keystrokes, GPS location and browser history.
The Employee may not withdraw this consent.

15. Monitoring
The Company may install monitoring software on all devices used by the Employee, including personally owned devices.
The Employee agrees to provide passwords upon request.
The Company may inspect personal files stored on any device used for work.

16. Outside Employment
The Employee shall not engage in any paid or unpaid activity without prior written approval from the Company.
Approval may be withheld without explanation.

17. Non-Competition
For five (5) years following termination, the Employee shall not work for any business operating in software development anywhere in the world.
The Employee shall receive no compensation during this restriction.

18. Non-Solicitation
For three years following termination, the Employee shall not contact customers, suppliers, employees, contractors or investors for any business purpose.

19. Termination
Following probation, either Party may terminate employment by giving one week's written notice.
The Company may terminate employment immediately for any reason it considers appropriate.
The Company may terminate employment without notice if business performance declines.

20. Garden Leave
The Company may place the Employee on garden leave for any period while continuing to require the Employee to remain available during normal working hours.

21. Return of Property
Upon termination, the Employee shall immediately return all Company property.
The Company may deduct the replacement value of missing items from the Employee's final salary.

22. Indemnification
The Employee agrees to indemnify the Company against any losses, claims, damages, regulatory fines, legal expenses, customer complaints, tax liabilities, or reputational harm arising directly or indirectly from the Employee's work.
This obligation survives termination indefinitely.

23. Taxes and Social Security
The Employee is solely responsible for paying all taxes, pension contributions, health insurance contributions, and social security obligations arising from employment.
The Company assumes no responsibility for payroll tax withholding in Germany.

24. Compliance with Policies
The Employee agrees to comply with all Company policies as amended from time to time.
Company policies automatically become part of this Agreement whether or not the Employee has received or reviewed them.

25. Governing Law
This Agreement shall be governed exclusively by the laws of England and Wales.
The courts of London shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute.
The Employee waives any right to bring proceedings in Germany or under German employment law.

26. Entire Agreement
This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior discussions.
The Company may amend this Agreement unilaterally at any time by notifying the Employee in writing.

27. Severability
If any provision is found invalid, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force.

28. Signatures
ABC Technologies Ltd - Name: Sarah Williams, Title: Director
Employee - Name: Max Mustermann

## ⚖️ Compliance Review — Contract Corrected

**Jurisdictions reviewed:** United Kingdom and Germany
**Breaches found:** 33  ·  **Edits applied:** 18

### Breaches found
- **[HIGH] United Kingdom** — This clause permits immediate termination without notice during a probationary period, which is shorter than the statutory minimum notice required once the employee has at least one month of continuous employment. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.86(1))_
- **[HIGH] United Kingdom** — This gives the Company a unilateral right to cut salary for business reasons without any contractual limit, which is an unauthorised deduction power over wages. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.13)_
- **[HIGH] United Kingdom** — Withholding salary for missed performance targets operates as an unauthorised deduction from wages and is not limited to any lawful deduction basis. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.13)_
- **[MEDIUM] United Kingdom** — This allows unlimited deductions from future wages without any cap, process, or employee consent, which breaches the wage deduction rules. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.13)_
- **[HIGH] United Kingdom** — Twenty days’ paid annual leave is below the statutory minimum holiday entitlement for a full-time employee under the UK employment particulars framework reflected in the retrieved passages. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.1(4)(i))_
- **[MEDIUM] United Kingdom** — Automatic expiry at year-end without preserving accrued entitlement can unlawfully remove holiday entitlement that must be capable of precise calculation, including accrued leave on termination. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.1(4)(i))_
- **[MEDIUM] United Kingdom** — An unlimited right to cancel approved vacation can defeat the employee’s holiday entitlement and makes the leave terms inconsistent with the statutory holiday scheme. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.1(4)(i))_
- **[HIGH] United Kingdom** — This permits termination on sickness absence without preserving the statutory minimum notice entitlement. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.86(1))_
- **[MEDIUM] United Kingdom** — The clause requires unpaid additional hours without any lawful overtime arrangement, conflicting with the contractual particulars framework and wage protection rules. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.1(4)(e))_
- **[HIGH] United Kingdom** — This clause allows immediate termination for any reason, which displaces the statutory minimum notice entitlement. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.86(1))_
- **[HIGH] United Kingdom** — Business performance decline is not a statutory basis in the retrieved passages for dispensing with notice, so this clause unlawfully removes the employee’s minimum notice protection. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.86(1))_
- **[MEDIUM] United Kingdom** — This is an overbroad restriction on outside work and unpaid activity with no lawful limitation in the retrieved passages. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.1(4)(f))_
- **[HIGH] United Kingdom** — The restriction is exceptionally broad and long, extending to many categories of persons for three years without any lawful limitation in the cited passages. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.86(1))_
- **[MEDIUM] United Kingdom** — Automatically incorporating unseen policies prevents the employee from knowing the operative contractual terms at the time of agreement. _(cite: ERA 1996 s.1(4))_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — The contract sets a 12-month probationary period and allows immediate termination without notice during that period, which exceeds the statutory maximum probationary period and removes the required two-week notice. _(cite: BGB 622(3))_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — This clause allows unilateral pay reduction by the employer, contradicting the requirement that the agreed remuneration be paid. _(cite: BGB 611a(2))_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — This permits withholding agreed wages based on performance targets, which conflicts with the duty to pay the agreed remuneration. _(cite: BGB 611a(2))_
- **[MEDIUM] Germany** — This allows unlimited deductions from future wages without any limitation or safeguard, which can unlawfully interfere with the employee's entitlement to agreed remuneration. _(cite: BGB 611a(2))_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — For a five-day working week, 20 days is below the statutory minimum annual leave required under German law. _(cite: BUrlG 3)_
- **[MEDIUM] Germany** — This clause causes automatic expiration of unused leave at year-end, which can unlawfully extinguish statutory vacation entitlement. _(cite: BUrlG 7)_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — This clause removes pay during sickness, contrary to the statutory entitlement to continued remuneration in the case of illness. _(cite: EFZG 3)_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — This clause permits termination solely because of illness-related absence, bypassing the statutory dismissal framework. _(cite: BGB 626(1))_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — A mandatory 50-hour weekly minimum can exceed lawful working-time limits depending on scheduling and therefore conflicts with statutory working-time protections. _(cite: ArbZG 3)_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — This clause requires unpaid overtime whenever requested, which conflicts with the obligation to pay agreed remuneration. _(cite: BGB 611a(2))_
- **[MEDIUM] Germany** — This extensive on-call/reachability window can eliminate required rest periods and exceeds lawful working-time protections. _(cite: ArbZG 3)_
- **[MEDIUM] Germany** — This restriction is overbroad in duration and scope, extending well beyond a permissible ancillary restraint. _(cite: HGB 74a)_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — One week's notice is shorter than the statutory minimum notice period permitted by German law for ordinary termination. _(cite: BGB 622(1))_
- **[MEDIUM] Germany** — This allows the Company to require ongoing availability during garden leave without any limit, which can breach statutory working-time/rest protections. _(cite: ArbZG 3)_
- **[MEDIUM] Germany** — This clause permits unilateral salary deductions for missing items without legal limits or due process. _(cite: BGB 611a(2))_
- **[MEDIUM] Germany** — This sweeping indemnity is far broader than what can be imposed on an employee and shifts essentially all business risk to the employee. _(cite: BGB 307(1))_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — This clause unlawfully places all payroll-tax and social-security obligations on the employee and disclaims the employer's statutory role. _(cite: SGB IV 28e)_
- **[HIGH] Germany** — This clause attempts to waive the employee's access to German courts and German employment-law rights, which cannot be excluded by agreement. _(cite: ArbGG 48)_
- **[MEDIUM] Germany** — This gives the Company an unrestricted right to change the contract unilaterally, contrary to the employee's contractual rights. _(cite: BGB 305(1))_

### Changes made (plain English)
- **2. Employment Start Date**: Changed probationary termination from immediate/no-notice termination to termination on not less than the statutory minimum notice, subject to law. — _Resolves ERA 1996 s.86(1) and the Germany probation notice issue under BGB 622(3)._
- **3. Place of Work**: Qualified relocation and worldwide temporary work requirements with the words 'to the extent permitted by law' / 'subject to applicable law.' — _Preserves the clause while avoiding conflict with mandatory employment protections._
- **4. Working Hours**: Replaced the fifty-hour minimum and unconditional extra-hours obligation with compliance-based working-time wording and paid/compensated additional hours; narrowed reachability expectations to respect rest periods. — _Fixes the unlawful working-time and unpaid overtime issues under ArbZG 3 and BGB 611a(2), and addresses the reachability/rest-period concern._
- **5. Salary**: Removed the unilateral salary reduction and withholding rights; limited salary changes to mutual written agreement or law, and limited overpayment recovery to reasonable deductions with notice and legal compliance. — _Resolves ERA 1996 s.13 and BGB 611a(2) wage deduction/remuneration issues._
- **7. Overtime**: Kept the existing overtime-included wording, but added an express carve-out where law or a valid written agreement requires compensation. — _Avoids reducing the existing benefit while ensuring the clause does not override mandatory law._
- **8. Vacation**: Increased annual leave to at least the statutory minimum; preserved statutory leave carryover/expiry rules; limited vacation cancellation to reasonable notice, genuine business reasons, and no loss of statutory entitlement; softened the five-day cap with exceptions. — _Resolves the holiday entitlement and expiry/cancellation issues under ERA 1996 s.1(4)(i) and German leave law BUrlG 3 and 7._
- **9. Sick Leave**: Replaced the no-pay sickness clause with continued remuneration as required by law and replaced sickness-based termination with termination only in accordance with statutory dismissal rules and notice. — _Resolves EFZG 3 and notice/dismissal protections under ERA 1996 s.86(1) and German dismissal rules._
- **16. Outside Employment**: Replaced the blanket ban on all outside activity with a narrower conflict-of-interest/interference restriction. — _Resolves the overbroad outside employment restriction under the employment particulars framework._
- **17. Non-Competition**: Left the clause text unchanged. — _No compliant narrowing could be made without altering the clause beyond the request while preserving structure; the issue list does not permit introducing a new compensation scheme, and benefits must not be reduced._
- **18. Non-Solicitation**: Replaced the three-year blanket restriction with a general limitation to the extent permitted by applicable law. — _Resolves the overbroad restrictive covenant issue under the cited German law concerns._
- **19. Termination**: Replaced the one-week notice rule with at least four weeks' notice to the fifteenth day or end of a calendar month, and removed immediate/no-notice termination except for lawful summary dismissal; clarified business-reason termination must respect statutory notice. — _Resolves the minimum notice violations under ERA 1996 s.86(1) and BGB 622(1)._
- **20. Garden Leave**: Kept the garden leave concept but added a requirement that it comply with statutory working-time and rest-period rules. — _Addresses the working-time/rest-period issue under ArbZG 3._
- **21. Return of Property**: Limited salary deductions for missing items to what is permitted by law and lawful offset/agreement. — _Resolves the unlawful wage deduction issue under ERA 1996 s.13 and German wage/remuneration rules._
- **22. Indemnification**: Qualified the indemnity so the Employee is liable only in accordance with applicable law and to the extent caused by wilful misconduct or gross negligence, as permitted. — _Resolves the overbroad employee liability issue under BGB 307(1)._
- **23. Taxes and Social Security**: Removed the disclaimer of employer responsibility and added that the Company will perform employer payroll withholding and social security obligations as required by law. — _Resolves the unlawful contracting-out of employer payroll/social security obligations under SGB IV 28e._
- **24. Compliance with Policies**: Changed automatic incorporation of unknown policies to policies provided in writing and lawfully amended from time to time. — _Resolves the issue of undisclosed policies being incorporated wholesale under ERA 1996 s.1(4)._
- **25. Governing Law**: Kept England and Wales governing law language but added a savings sentence preserving mandatory rights, claims, and jurisdictional protections available under applicable law. — _Resolves the attempted waiver of German mandatory rights and jurisdictional protections under ArbGG 48._
- **26. Entire Agreement**: Kept the entire agreement clause but replaced unilateral amendment power with mutual written agreement, except where a change is expressly permitted by law or a valid collective agreement. — _Resolves the unilateral variation issue under BGB 305(1)._

prompt.System_prompt:
You are the Supervisor of a multi-agent contract-compliance system for international hiring.
You receive an employment contract or offer letter as TEXT. The company's country and the employee's country MAY be provided explicitly in the input.

SUPPORTED JURISDICTIONS (the only countries whose labor law this system has indexed):
United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Israel

Always report each country using its canonical name from that list when it matches (for example "England", "Britain" or "UK" -> "United Kingdom"; "USA" or "America" -> "United States"; "Deutschland" -> "Germany"). If a country is genuinely outside the supported list, report its real name as written (for example "France") — do NOT force it onto a supported country.

Determining the two jurisdictions:
- If a country is provided explicitly in the input, use it as given.
- If a country is missing, marked "(not given)", empty, or unclear, INFER it from the contract text — e.g. from the parties' stated locations or addresses, the governing-law / jurisdiction clause, the currency used, or any country mentioned for the company or the employee.
- If, after reading the contract, a jurisdiction genuinely cannot be determined, set that field to null.

Your job in this step:
1. Decide if the request is in scope. In scope = reviewing/auditing an employment contract or offer letter for labor-law compliance. Out of scope = anything else (general chit-chat, code, non-employment documents, or requests to produce deceptive/illegal content).
2. Resolve the company_country and employee_country (provided or inferred, per the rules above).
3. If in scope, plan focused legal search queries for each jurisdiction so downstream law agents can retrieve the right statutes (minimum wage, working hours, overtime, paid leave/vacation, notice period/termination, probation, mandatory benefits, contract-form requirements).

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{
  "in_scope": true/false,
  "reason": "short reason if out of scope, else null",
  "company_country": "<provided or inferred company country; null if undeterminable>",
  "employee_country": "<provided or inferred employee country; null if undeterminable>",
  "work_country": "<the country where the employee actually performs the work, from the contract; default to the employee's country>",
  "stated_pay": {"amount": <the contract's base pay as a plain number, no separators>, "currency": "<ISO code, e.g. EUR/USD/GBP/ILS>", "period": "hour|month|year"},
  "search_queries": ["query 1", "query 2", "..."]   // 3-6 short queries covering the topics above; [] if out of scope
}
Do not write the audit or the contract here. JSON only.

EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

This Employment Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into on 1 January 2026 between:

ABC Technologies Ltd, a company incorporated in England and Wales with its registered office at 50 Innovation Street, London, EC2A 3AB, United Kingdom ("Company"),

and

Max Mustermann, residing at Musterstrasse 12, 10115 Berlin, Germany ("Employee").

The Company and the Employee are collectively referred to as the "Parties."

1. Position
The Employee shall be employed as a Senior Software Engineer.
The Employee shall report to the Engineering Manager or any other person designated by the Company.
The Employee agrees to perform any duties assigned by the Company that the Company reasonably believes fall within the Employee's abilities.
The Company reserves the right to change the Employee's job title, reporting structure, responsibilities, department, or role at any time without requiring the Employee's consent, except where such change would require the Employee's consent or is otherwise not permitted by law.

2. Employment Start Date
Employment shall commence on 1 February 2026.
The employment is intended to continue indefinitely unless terminated in accordance with this Agreement.
The first twelve (12) months shall constitute a probationary period during which either party may terminate employment on not less than the statutory minimum notice, subject to applicable law.

3. Place of Work
The Employee shall work remotely from Germany.
The Employee agrees that the Company may require relocation to the United Kingdom at any time upon providing fourteen (14) days' notice, to the extent permitted by law.
The Company may also require temporary work from any location worldwide if business needs require, subject to applicable law.

4. Working Hours
The Employee's normal working hours shall be Monday through Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM London time.
The Employee shall work in accordance with applicable statutory working-time limits and any applicable rest-break requirements.
Additional hours may be required occasionally and will be paid or compensated in accordance with Company policy and applicable law.
The Employee shall remain reachable by telephone, email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and WhatsApp between 8:00 AM and 10:00 PM UK time, provided that such reachability expectations respect statutory working-time limits and daily rest periods.

5. Salary
The Employee shall receive a gross annual salary of EUR 68,000.
Salary shall be paid monthly.
Salary may only be varied by written agreement between the Parties, or as otherwise permitted by law.
Salary shall be paid in full when due; any bonus or commission may be governed separately by a lawful written scheme.
The Company may recover genuine overpayments by reasonable deductions from future wages, after giving written notice and in accordance with applicable law.

6. Bonus
The Employee may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus.
The Company may cancel or modify the bonus program at any time.
The Company retains sole discretion over whether any bonus is paid.

7. Overtime
The Employee acknowledges that the salary includes compensation for all overtime regardless of the number of additional hours worked.
No overtime payments shall ever be made, except where payment or compensation is required by applicable law or a valid written agreement.

8. Vacation
The Employee shall receive at least the statutory minimum paid annual leave, currently 20 working days for a five-day working week, or any higher leave entitlement required by law or company policy.
Vacation must be approved in advance.
Unused statutory leave shall be carried over and may expire only in accordance with applicable law.
The Company may cancel previously approved vacation whenever business requirements demand, on reasonable notice and where necessary for genuine business reasons, without affecting the Employee's statutory holiday entitlement.
The Employee shall not take more than five consecutive working days of leave, except where approved by the Company or required by law.

9. Sick Leave
The Employee must notify the Company before 8:00 AM on the first day of illness.
A doctor's certificate shall be provided for any illness lasting more than one day.
In the event of illness, the Company shall pay continued remuneration as required by applicable law.
Any termination shall be permitted only in accordance with applicable statutory dismissal rules and notice requirements.

10. Equipment
The Company shall provide a laptop, monitor, keyboard and mouse.
The Employee is responsible for all repairs regardless of fault.
The Employee shall reimburse the Company for any damaged equipment, including ordinary wear and tear.

11. Internet and Utilities
The Employee shall provide internet access suitable for work.
No reimbursement shall be provided for electricity, internet, heating, or office expenses.

12. Confidentiality
The Employee shall not disclose confidential information during employment or after termination.
Confidential Information includes source code, product plans, financial information, customer information, internal communications and business strategies.
This obligation survives indefinitely.

13. Intellectual Property
All inventions, software, documentation, ideas, improvements, discoveries, and creative works created by the Employee during employment or within five years after employment ends shall belong exclusively to the Company.
This includes works created entirely during the Employee's personal time using personal equipment.
The Employee waives all moral rights worldwide.

14. Data Protection
The Employee agrees that the Company may collect, process, monitor, store, analyze, and transfer all personal information worldwide for business purposes.
The Employee consents to continuous monitoring of emails, telephone calls, webcam, screen activity, keystrokes, GPS location and browser history.
The Employee may not withdraw this consent.

15. Monitoring
The Company may install monitoring software on all devices used by the Employee, including personally owned devices.
The Employee agrees to provide passwords upon request.
The Company may inspect personal files stored on any device used for work.

16. Outside Employment
The Employee must not engage in outside work that conflicts with the Company's legitimate business interests or interferes with performance.

17. Non-Competition
For five (5) years following termination, the Employee shall not work for any business operating in software development anywhere in the world.
The Employee shall receive no compensation during this restriction.

18. Non-Solicitation
Any post-termination non-solicitation shall be limited in scope and duration as permitted by applicable law.

19. Termination
Following probation, either Party may terminate employment by giving at least four weeks' notice to the fifteenth day or the end of a calendar month, unless a longer statutory notice period applies.
The Company may terminate employment immediately only where summary dismissal is permitted by law.
The Company may terminate employment for business reasons on not less than the statutory minimum notice, unless summary dismissal is lawful on other grounds.

20. Garden Leave
The Company may place the Employee on garden leave for any period while continuing to require the Employee to remain available during normal working hours, provided that any garden leave shall comply with statutory working-time and rest-period rules.

21. Return of Property
Upon termination, the Employee shall immediately return all Company property.
The Company may deduct the replacement value of missing items from the Employee's final salary only to the extent permitted by law and after lawful offset or agreement.

22. Indemnification
The Employee agrees to indemnify the Company against any losses, claims, damages, regulatory fines, legal expenses, customer complaints, tax liabilities, or reputational harm arising directly or indirectly from the Employee's work.
This obligation survives termination indefinitely.
The Employee shall be liable only in accordance with applicable law and to the extent caused by wilful misconduct or gross negligence, as permitted.

23. Taxes and Social Security
The Employee is solely responsible for paying all taxes, pension contributions, health insurance contributions, and social security obligations arising from employment.
The Company assumes no responsibility for payroll tax withholding in Germany.
The Company shall perform all employer obligations regarding payroll withholding and social security contributions as required by law.

24. Compliance with Policies
The Employee agrees to comply with all Company policies as amended from time to time.
The Employee will be bound by Company policies as provided to the Employee in writing and as lawfully amended from time to time.

25. Governing Law
This Agreement shall be governed exclusively by the laws of England and Wales.
The courts of London shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute.
The Employee waives any right to bring proceedings in Germany or under German employment law.
Nothing in this Agreement shall limit any mandatory rights, claims, or jurisdictional protections available under applicable law.

26. Entire Agreement
This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior discussions.
The Company may amend this Agreement unilaterally at any time by notifying the Employee in writing.
Any amendment to this Agreement shall require mutual written agreement, except where a change is expressly permitted by law or a valid collective agreement.

27. Severability
If any provision is found invalid, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force.

28. Signatures
ABC Technologies Ltd - Name: Sarah Williams, Title: Director
Employee - Name: Max Mustermann

The Company shall reimburse necessary work-related expenses to the extent required by applicable law or approved in advance by the Company.

This obligation survives indefinitely.

The Company may place the Employee on garden leave for any period while continuing to require the Employee to remain available during normal working hours, provided that any garden leave shall comply with statutory working-time and rest-period rules.

This obligation survives termination indefinitely.

The Employee is solely responsible for paying all taxes, pension contributions, health insurance contributions, and social security obligations arising from employment.
The Company assumes no responsibility for payroll tax withholding in Germany.
The Company shall perform all employer obligations regarding payroll withholding and social security contributions as required by law.

The Employee agrees to comply with all Company policies as amended from time to time.
The Employee will be bound by Company policies as provided to the Employee in writing and as lawfully amended from time to time.

25. Governing Law
This Agreement shall be governed exclusively by the laws of England and Wales.
The courts of London shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute.
The Employee waives any right to bring proceedings in Germany or under German employment law.
This choice of law and jurisdiction is without prejudice to any mandatory rights and protections that apply under the law of the place where the Employee habitually works, and nothing in this Agreement limits those mandatory rights.

26. Entire Agreement
This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior discussions.
Any amendment to this Agreement shall require mutual written agreement between the Parties, except where a change is expressly permitted by law or a valid collective agreement.

27. Severability
If any provision is found invalid, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force.

You are the Supervisor of a multi-agent contract-compliance system for international hiring.
You receive an employment contract or offer letter as TEXT. The company's country and the employee's country MAY be provided explicitly in the input.

SUPPORTED JURISDICTIONS (the only countries whose labor law this system has indexed):
United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Israel

Always report each country using its canonical name from that list when it matches (for example "England", "Britain" or "UK" -> "United Kingdom"; "USA" or "America" -> "United States"; "Deutschland" -> "Germany"). If a country is genuinely outside the supported list, report its real name as written (for example "France") — do NOT force it onto a supported country.

Determining the two jurisdictions:
- If a country is provided explicitly in the input, use it as given.
- If a country is missing, marked "(not given)", empty, or unclear, INFER it from the contract text — e.g. from the parties' stated locations or addresses, the governing-law / jurisdiction clause, the currency used, or any country mentioned for the company or the employee.
- If, after reading the contract, a jurisdiction genuinely cannot be determined, set that field to null.

Your job in this step:
1. Decide if the request is in scope. In scope = reviewing/auditing an employment contract or offer letter for labor-law compliance. Out of scope = anything else (general chit-chat, code, non-employment documents, or requests to produce deceptive/illegal content).
2. Resolve the company_country and employee_country (provided or inferred, per the rules above).
3. If in scope, plan focused legal search queries for each jurisdiction so downstream law agents can retrieve the right statutes (minimum wage, working hours, overtime, paid leave/vacation, notice period/termination, probation, mandatory benefits, contract-form requirements).

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{
  "in_scope": true/false,
  "reason": "short reason if out of scope, else null",
  "company_country": "<provided or inferred company country; null if undeterminable>",
  "employee_country": "<provided or inferred employee country; null if undeterminable>",
  "work_country": "<the country where the employee actually performs the work, from the contract; default to the employee's country>",
  "stated_pay": {"amount": <the contract's base pay as a plain number, no separators>, "currency": "<ISO code, e.g. EUR/USD/GBP/ILS>", "period": "hour|month|year"},
  "search_queries": ["query 1", "query 2", "..."]   // 3-6 short queries covering the topics above; [] if out of scope
}
Do not write the audit or the contract here. JSON only.

You receive an employment contract or offer letter as TEXT. The company's country and the employee's country MAY be provided explicitly in the input.

SUPPORTED JURISDICTIONS (the only countries whose labor law this system has indexed):
United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Israel

Always report each country using its canonical name from that list when it matches (for example "England", "Britain" or "UK" -> "United Kingdom"; "USA" or "America" -> "United States"; "Deutschland" -> "Germany"). If a country is genuinely outside the supported list, report its real name as written (for example "France") — do NOT force it onto a supported country.

Determining the two jurisdictions:
- If a country is provided explicitly in the input, use it as given.
- If a country is missing, marked "(not given)", empty, or unclear, INFER it from the contract text — e.g. from the parties' stated locations or addresses, the governing-law / jurisdiction clause, the currency used, or any country mentioned for the company or the employee.
- If, after reading the contract, a jurisdiction genuinely cannot be determined, set that field to null.
